key_insight: Patient-separated, label-corrected evaluation overturned the benchmark’s conclusions: no tested imbalance strategy improved observed mean macro F2 by more than 0.01 over no augmentation.
clinical_relevance: Reliable assessment of multimodal chest X-ray models requires preventing patient overlap and aligning diagnostic labels with the relevant admission before considering clinical use.
method: Audited record-level splits using an EHR-based label lookup and unseen-patient testing.
Traced diagnosis labels to source admissions and evaluated admission-aligned, rule-refined labels.
Compared imbalance strategies, classifiers, diagnostic history and image embeddings under patient-separated evaluation.
evidence_signal: Across 29,083 radiographs from 10,479 patients with eight diagnosis targets, the lookup nearly matched the best record-split model, while every model fell to all-positive baseline performance on unseen patients.
watch_item: Encoder comparisons require pretraining-overlap checks: RAD-DINO had seen 96.6% of these radiographs during self-supervised pretraining.
paper_title: Leakage- and Label-Aware Benchmarking of Class-Imbalance Strategies for Multimodal Chest X-Ray and EHR Classification
